title: SELinux without fear
subtitle: The second permission system on RHEL — plus a firewall and SSH baseline that stays on.
objectives: Explain SELinux modes and security contexts
Read a denial and find the right fix
Restore a file context without disabling enforcement
Apply practical SSH and firewall hardening
Build a small, repeatable security baseline

sections.title: SELinux is not a permissions bug
Read the denial, then fix the cause

commands.desc: Show SELinux policy, mode, and status.
Show processes with their SELinux domains.
Allow a service domain to bind a custom port.

lab.title: Keep SELinux enforcing
lab.scenario: Deploy content into a web root and diagnose a context mismatch without turning off the control.

steps.text: Confirm SELinux is enforcing and record the current mode.
steps.verify: getenforce should print Enforcing, and sestatus should confirm the targeted policy.

steps.cmd: sudo dnf install -y httpd && sudo systemctl enable --now httpd && systemctl is-active httpd
steps.verify: systemctl is-active httpd should print active.

steps.text: Create content in /var/www/html and inspect its context.
steps.cmd: echo "hello from RHEL" | sudo tee /var/www/html/index.html && ls -Z /var/www/html/index.html
steps.verify: ls -Z should show httpd_sys_content_t for the new index.html.

steps.text: Copy a file from your home directory into the web root and compare contexts.
steps.verify: The copied file may retain a home-directory type such as user_home_t.

steps.text: Restore the correct web content context and verify.
steps.verify: The file should now be httpd_sys_content_t.

steps.text: Check for denials and inspect the firewall.
steps.cmd: sudo ausearch -m AVC -ts recent; sudo firewall-cmd --list-all
steps.verify: ausearch should show no recent AVC denials, and firewall-cmd should list the public zone.

quiz.q: What should you try before setting SELinux to permissive?
options: Read the AVC denial and fix the context, port, or boolean
quiz.why: The denial identifies the mismatch. Correcting it preserves protection and fixes the actual cause.

quiz.q: Which command restores policy-defined contexts under /var/www/html?
quiz.why: restorecon applies the expected SELinux context. chmod and chown do not change SELinux labels.

quiz.q: Why validate SSH configuration with sshd -t before reloading?
options: It catches syntax errors before they can lock you out
quiz.why: sshd -t checks the configuration. A bad config plus a restart can remove your remote access.
